ratings.excerpt: Undemanding and uplifting old-school showbiz fun … This celebration of Jerry Herman, the man behind Hello Dolly! and La Cage Aux Folles, at London’s Menier Chocolate Factory is energising … The production is modest but still redolent of greasepaint and glamour. We are in a vintage, rather than modern, theatre. … The songs are neatly distributed among Cassidy Janson, Jessica Martin and Julie Yammanee to capitalise on their respective personalities: sophisticated, seasoned and perky. … There is a lot to like here, including Matt Cole’s consistently adept choreography and the sparkling accompaniment of the six-piece, all-female band. And above all, of course, there is the energy and emotional pull of Herman’s indelible music.

Thoughtfully constructed revue of Jerry Herman hits gets a bravura delivery … Hannah Chissick’s revival navigates a very specific path though the numbers. With the help of designer Paul Farnsworth, Chissick places her trio of vocalists – Cassidy Janson, Jessica Martin and Julie Yammanee – in a shared dressing room at a theatre. … There’s no dialogue, but Chissick unearths the drama or comedy in each song to feed her narrative. … It’s Martin, however, who really takes an emotional journey. She’s funny and self-deprecating with Take It All Off or La Cage Aux Folles, contemplative in Before the Parade Passes By, and hits her stride with a revelatory I Don’t Want to Know. … Chissick’s production, with accompaniment from musical director Sarah Travis and her melodious all-woman band, is a salie

Three stalwart performers belt their way through Jerry Herman's hits and misses … Much of this feels like it was written by AI fed on 1930s Tinseltown cliches … Herman specialised in “the simple, hummable song … All three women, sorry “girls … The three fraught songs from Dear World, written for Angela Lansbury who’d starred in Mame, are turgid. Inevitably it’s the tunes from La Cage and Hello, Dolly! – Before the Parade Passes By, It Only Takes a Minute, Just Leave Everything to Me – that come across best.
